page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is limited to 8.0 GB, yielding a RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance but weaker multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1620.59, while the multi-core test scored 3324.57. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with a Passmark memory score of 989.87 and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 27.54 GB/sec. However, the CPU features advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which support specialized workloads. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression (25.97 GB/sec) and text processing perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (20.97 GB/sec) is poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highcpu-4 offers a dense compute profile for workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The low RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. Instead, it is best suited for compute-bound, single-threaded or lightly threaded applications, basic web serving (achieving a static web serving throughput of 6.78 GB/sec), and lightweight LLM inference tasks utilizing small models.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 2 physical cores with hyper-threading and lacks local storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1635.0, but weaker multi-core and memory performance, illustrated by a Passmark memory score in the bottom 10%. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX), which assist with specialized instruction sets. Qualitatively, this instance is a cost-effective choice for compute-heavy, low-memory tasks. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing, and small-scale model inference.
